source: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 20 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 20
knowledgePattern: Design an adaptive distinguishing query and prove no single query can suffice
solution:
The two zero responses rule out {a,f} in position 1, {b,e} in position 2, {a,c} in position 3, d in position 4, {b,e} in position 5, and {c,f} in position 6.

In fbdcae the first two positions are already impossible. Exactly three of its final four positions must therefore match. Split into the four cases according to which of positions 3–6 fails, and fill the remaining places with unused letters subject to the exclusions.

The failed position 3 gives bdfcae or dfbcae; failed position 4 gives bcdfae or cfdbae; failed position 5 gives badcfe; failed position 6 gives efdcab. These are all six candidates.

Any two candidates agree in at least two positions, as direct comparison of the list shows. Under any one trial string, positions where the candidates agree contribute equally to their scores. Their scores can therefore differ by at most four. Thus the six scores lie within five consecutive integer values, so at least two candidates have the same response. One further trial cannot guarantee identification.

Two suffice. Try abcfde. In the order badcfe, bcdfae, bdfcae, cfdbae, dfbcae, efdcab, the responses are 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 0. A response of 0 or 2 identifies the password immediately. A response of 1 leaves badcfe, bdfcae, cfdbae, dfbcae.

For that remaining group, try baecdf. The respective responses are 3, 2, 0, 1, all different, so the password is now identified. The lower bound and this adaptive strategy agree: N = 2, answer B. Identification is what is required; there is no need for another trial merely to enter an already known password.

hints.title: Use each zero response position by position
hints.body: List which letters are forbidden in each position, then compare those restrictions with the third attempt.
hints.recap: A complete case split uses every supplied condition and does not omit allowed configurations.
hints.pitfall: A response counts matching positions, not how many letters occur somewhere in the password.
hints.pause: Determine which positions of the third attempt can possibly contribute to its response.

recall.reminder: A complete case split uses every supplied condition and does not omit allowed configurations.

hints.title: Enumerate only the remaining cases
hints.body: Choose which still-possible positions match the third attempt, then fill all other positions using the unused letters and the zero-response restrictions.
hints.recap: Cases must exhaust the possibilities while respecting all distinctness restrictions.
hints.pitfall: A trial used to gather information need not itself be one of the remaining possible passwords.
hints.pause: Make and verify the complete list of remaining passwords.

recall.reminder: Cases must exhaust the possibilities while respecting all distinctness restrictions.

hints.title: Prove a lower bound on information
hints.body: Compare pairs of remaining candidates: positions where they agree contribute equally to their responses under any trial. Use this to bound how far apart response scores can be.
hints.recap: To prove a smallest guarantee, first rule out every strategy using fewer observations.
hints.pitfall: A trial that succeeds for one lucky password does not establish a guarantee for every password.
hints.pause: Decide how many candidates a single response can distinguish in the worst case.

recall.reminder: To prove a smallest guarantee, first rule out every strategy using fewer observations.

hints.title: Build a strategy for every response group
hints.body: Try trial strings that split the candidate list into response groups. For any group still containing several candidates, seek a later trial with distinct responses within that group.
hints.recap: A bound is attained only when an explicit construction works in every allowed case.
hints.pitfall: Later trials may depend on the response already received; count the longest branch of your strategy.
hints.pause: Give a strategy covering every possible response and compare its worst-case number of trials with your lower bound.

recall.reminder: A bound is attained only when an explicit construction works in every allowed case.
